headline: 18:40 Zurich: a sharp relief bounce in the last hour; gold jumps about 1.5% (a five-sigma hourly move), the S&P 500 halves its loss to about -1.3% and the dollar eases, but VIX is still near 31

findings.headline: Gold and stocks snap back in the past hour as the dollar eases
findings.body: Gold rose about 1.5-1.7% in an hour to near 3,527, roughly five times its usual hourly swing, after touching about 3,440 earlier; it is still down about 1.8% on the day. The S&P 500 has climbed back to near 7,107, cutting its loss to about 1.3% from 3.1% at 15:45, and copper is up about 1.3% in the hour. EUR/USD briefly jumped about 0.35% to 1.099 as the dollar index slipped about 0.25%, though that move has since faded. The US 10-year yield holds near 4.83%, about 8bp lower on the day, and VIX has eased to about 31 but remains up some 18%, so this reads as short-covering after the morning's cash-raising rather than an all-clear; we found no single headline behind it.

sources.label: Benzinga: Gold down 3%; midday market summary

findings.headline: Sticky core and strong growth: a December hike is settled, 2027 is now the debate
findings.body: Headline PCE matched forecasts at 3.8%, but core came in at 3.3% against 3.2% expected, while Q3 GDP was revised up to 4.3% annualised from 3.4% and jobless claims fell to 189,000. With growth this firm there is no case for the Fed to wait, and markets put the odds of a quarter-point hike on 8-9 December at about 93-98%, with talk now turning to further hikes next year. That Treasuries are catching a haven bid despite hot data says the equity sell-off, not inflation, is driving bonds today.

findings.headline: USTR's excess-capacity tariffs name Switzerland and the EU, not just China
findings.body: The US Trade Representative found against 14 economies and proposed tariffs of 15% on all EU goods, up to 15% on Swiss goods and up to 20% on most Chinese goods, net of existing duties and with exemptions. The Swiss findings explicitly cite holding down the franc and support for pharma, which makes SNB currency intervention politically costlier just as the franc rallies. Nothing takes effect yet: comments are due 5 January and hearings start 25 January 2027, so prices have only begun to weigh the risk for European and Swiss exporters.

findings.headline: The AI sell-off deepens into a financing story
findings.body: Nvidia lost about 8% in early trade and Anthropic slipped below its $83 IPO price, as investors questioned whether debt-funded data-centre spending will earn its cost. Hot inflation and a firmer Fed path raise the cost of that debt at the worst moment, which is why the selling has spread from chipmakers to the wider AI complex rather than staying a single-stock story.

sources.label: Reuters via Investing.com: AI stocks slide on fears over infrastructure buildout costs
Yahoo Finance: Stock market today, chip rout continues on hot inflation and new tariffs

view: Our view: The bounce shows the cash-raising phase may be easing, as gold steadying was the signal to watch, but VIX near 31 and a Fed hike all but certain for December mean it is fragile. A close well off the lows tonight would help; a reversal into a thin Thanksgiving session would say the de-risking is not done.
